criteria.description: Correctly splits A union B into three disjoint pieces and applies additivity.
Correctly derives p(A\B) and p(B\A) in terms of p(A), p(B), p(A∩B), and substitutes back.

solutions.fullSolution:
A union B = (A\B) union (B\A) union (A intersect B), a disjoint union. By additivity: p(A union B) = p(A\B) + p(B\A) + p(A intersect B).
A = (A\B) union (A intersect B), disjoint, so p(A) = p(A\B) + p(A intersect B), giving p(A\B) = p(A) - p(A intersect B). Similarly p(B\A) = p(B) - p(A intersect B).
Substitute: p(A union B) = [p(A)-p(A intersect B)] + [p(B)-p(A intersect B)] + p(A intersect B) = p(A)+p(B)-p(A intersect B).

criteria.description: Correctly distinguishes joint (both together), marginal (one ignoring the other), and conditional (one given a specific value of the other).
Correctly states how marginal (sum over joint) and conditional (slice + renormalize) are each computed from the joint.

commonErrors: Confusing marginal with conditional (or vice versa).
Forgetting the renormalization step (dividing by P(y)) when computing a conditional from a joint slice.

solutions.fullSolution: P(X,Y) describes X and Y together, the most complete description of their relationship. The marginal P(X) ignores Y entirely, obtained by summing the joint over all Y values: P(X)=sum_y P(X,y). The conditional P(X|Y=y) describes X given that Y is known to equal y specifically, obtained by taking the joint's slice at Y=y and renormalizing (dividing by P(y)=sum_x P(x,y)) so it sums to 1 over X.

criteria.description: Correctly rearranges both conditional-probability definitions to isolate P(A,B).
Correctly sets the two expressions for P(A,B) equal and divides through to get Bayes' rule.

commonErrors: Trying to derive this a different way (e.g. citing Bayes' rule as already known) rather than the requested direct algebraic route.
Sign or division errors when isolating P(A|B) at the end.

solutions.fullSolution: From P(A|B)=P(A,B)/P(B): P(A,B) = P(A|B)*P(B). From P(B|A)=P(A,B)/P(A): P(A,B) = P(B|A)*P(A). Both expressions equal the same joint P(A,B), so: P(A|B)*P(B) = P(B|A)*P(A). Dividing both sides by P(B): P(A|B) = P(B|A)*P(A)/P(B), Bayes' rule.

P(pos) = P(pos|disease)*P(disease) + P(pos|no disease)*P(no disease) = 0.9*0.02 + 0.1*0.98 = 0.018+0.098 = 0.116. P(disease|pos) = 0.018/0.116 = 0.1552. Despite a 90% true-positive rate, the posterior probability of disease given a positive test is only about 15.5%, because the disease is rare (2% prior) so false positives from the much larger healthy population outnumber true positives.
